Nodyn (Saesneg)

The last chapter adds no new grammar. It brings back the forms of Rhan 4 and closes the story, and it uses one small word a great deal: pan ('when').

Pan gives the soft mutation to the verb after it, if the verb can mutate. With oedd, which starts with a vowel, nothing changes: - About the past: Edrychodd Arthur ar ddrws y gegin, lle roedd e'n arfer cario dŵr pan oedd e'n fachgen bach ('Arthur looked at the kitchen door, where he used to carry water when he was a small boy'); Roedd gwynt oer yn dod ohoni hi, fel pan oedd Arthur yn hebog bach ('A cold wind was coming out of it, as when Arthur was a little hawk'); Gwelais i hi o'r awyr, pan o'n i'n hebog ('I saw it from the sky, when I was a hawk'). Pan gyrhaeddon nhw'r llys ('When they reached the court') shows the mutation: cyrhaeddon → gyrhaeddon. - About the future: bydd becomes fydd after pan. Myrddin prophesies: pan fydd angen brenin ar Gymru, byddi di'n deffro ('when Wales needs a king, you will wake up'). Dafi promises: A gwnaf i warchod Arthur hefyd, pan fydd e'n cysgu ('And I'll guard Arthur too, when he is sleeping'). Notice that English uses the present after 'when' ('when Wales needs', 'when he is sleeping'), but Welsh uses the future, bydd, because the event is in the future.

Do not confuse pan with two words that look or sound related. Pryd? asks 'when?' as a question: Ond Myrddin: pryd fydd yr amser yn dod? ('But Myrddin: when will the time come?'). And os means 'if', not 'when': A bydd Modlen yn gwneud brecwast i ti, os bydd hi'n deffro'n gynnar ('And Modlen will make you breakfast, if she wakes up early'). Myrddin is sure that the time will come, so he says pan; he is not sure that Modlen will wake early, so he says os.

Two old formulas appear for reading only. Pan ddaw'r amser means 'when the time comes'. Daw is the short future of dod for 'he' or 'it', which this book has not taught you to use; pan ddaw'r amser means the same as pan fydd yr amser yn dod. The title, Y brenin a fu ac a fydd, means 'the king who was and who will be'. It uses the relative a from Pennod 28 (y cleddyf a dynnodd Arth, 'the sword that Arth pulled'), followed by fu, an old past form of bod, and by fydd. In everyday words it is y brenin oedd, a'r brenin fydd.

Short forms from Pennod 37 return. Mali today says Af i i'r bryn gyda'r ci, Mam-gu. Dof i'n ôl cyn chwech! ('I'll go to the hill with the dog, Grandma. I'll come back before six!'); dof i is the 'I' form of dod. Dafi answers Myrddin's question Wnei di aros yma a gwarchod yr ogof i fi? ('Will you stay here and guard the cave for me?') with Gwnaf ('I will'), then Gwnaf i warchod yr ogof ('I'll guard the cave'), with the soft mutation after gwnaf i.

A few new words describe time and feeling. Henaint is 'old age': Mae henaint yn dod i bawb, hyd yn oed i ddewin ('Old age comes to everyone, even to a wizard'). Hiraeth is a longing for a place, a person or a time that is gone. You feel it: Teimlodd e hiraeth mawr am y dyddiau hynny ('He felt a great longing for those days'). Like ofn, it is 'on' a person: Bydd hiraeth arna i ('I will miss you', literally 'longing will be on me'). Erioed means 'ever, always (in the past)': Mae e wedi bod yma erioed ('It has always been here'). O hyd and yn dal both mean 'still': maen nhw'n cysgu yno o hyd ('they are still sleeping there'); Mae'r afon yn dal yno ('The river is still there'). Daeth … i ben means 'came to an end': Daeth amser Arthur a'i gwmni i ben ('The time of Arthur and his company came to an end').

The tables sum up Rhan 4, with one line from the story for each chapter: - 32: the past passive, Cafodd Arthur ei goroni gan yr esgob ('Arthur was crowned by the bishop'). - 33: reported speech, Dwedodd e fod Rhita'n gawr mawr iawn ('He said that Rhita was a very big giant'). - 34 and 37: the conditional, Taswn i'n gawr, baswn i'n chwerthin ('If I were a giant, I would laugh'); Basen nhw'n chwerthin ('They would laugh'). - 35: should, Dylai brenin arwain fel gŵydd ('A king should lead like a goose'). - 36: northern Welsh for reading, Mae gen i lefrith = Mae llaeth gyda fi ('I have milk'). - 37: short futures, Gwnaf i warchod yr ogof ('I'll guard the cave'). - 38: the present and future passive, Bydd hi'n cael ei chadw yn y cronicl ('It will be kept in the chronicle'), and the chronicle's gwelwyd ('was seen') for reading. - 39: y bydd, lle and ai, Dw i'n gwybod y bydd e'n dod ('I know that it will come'). The mutation table gathers the triggers that Rhan 4 used most: gan, a short future such as gwnaf i, mor and â, and pan.

Further mutation-table translations: gan ferch Cynyr means “by Cynyr’s daughter”; mor fach â llygoden means “as small as a mouse”; mor fawr â thŷ means “as big as a house”. The past and future labels describe tense, not specifically yesterday and tomorrow: this story ranges over many years.

  6. Mae Pero wrth y drws gwyrdd, wrth y tŵr. (Places Pero by the door or the tower, or on the path (s086).) Geiriau allweddol drws, gwyrdd, tŵr
  7. Mae e wrth y drws gwyrdd, yn y mwg. (Places the small red creature by the door or in the smoke.) Geiriau allweddol drws, mwg

  2. Myrddin yw'r hen ddyn. Dewin yw e. (Identifies the old man as Myrddin; saying that he is a wizard is optional.) Geiriau allweddol hen, dyn, dewin
  3. Dafi yw'r ddraig fach goch. (Says Dafi is the little (red) dragon.) Geiriau allweddol draig
  4. Mae Mali eisiau mynd i'r llys. (Says Mali wants to go to the llys.) Geiriau allweddol eisiau, llys

  6. Mae Dafi yn yr het. / Mae Dafi yn het Myrddin. (Says Dafi is in (Myrddin's) hat.) Geiriau allweddol het
  7. … dw i. (Introduces yourself in the first person (… dw i).) Geiriau allweddol bod

  7. Dw i'n bwyta brecwast yn y gegin. (Says where you eat breakfast, in the first person.) Geiriau allweddol bwyta, brecwast

Pensum C — Cwestiynau

  1. Mae rhywbeth yno sy'n aros am Arthur. (Mae rhywbeth yno sy'n aros am Arthur.) Geiriau allweddol aros
  2. Roedd e'n arfer cario dŵr. (Cario dŵr.) Geiriau allweddol pan, arfer
  3. Roedd bwrdd crwn o garreg yng nghanol yr ogof. (Bwrdd crwn o garreg.) Geiriau allweddol ogof, crwn
  4. Pan fydd angen brenin ar Gymru, byddi di'n deffro. (… bydd Arthur yn deffro (byddi di'n deffro).) Geiriau allweddol proffwydoliaeth, deffro
  5. "Gwnaf i warchod yr ogof. A gwnaf i warchod Arthur hefyd, pan fydd e'n cysgu." (Un peth: gwarchod yr ogof · gwarchod Arthur.) Geiriau allweddol gwarchod
  6. "Dim signal eto! Does byth signal ar y bryn yma." (Does dim signal.) Geiriau allweddol signal, bryn
  7. Mae Mali'n gweld cynffon fach goch a dau lygad mawr, melyn. (Un peth: cynffon fach goch · dau lygad melyn.) Geiriau allweddol ogof
  8. Pan fydd hi'n bwrw glaw, bydda i'n darllen llyfr. (Pan fydd …, bydda i'n ….) Geiriau allweddol pan
